content.actor.captain.name: 卫队长
content.area.castle.name: 杜恩城堡
content.class.visitor.blurb: 一本导览手册，一架单筒望远镜留着上城墙步道，还有一整个下午。
content.class.visitor.kit.0.name: 导览手册
content.class.visitor.kit.1.name: 单筒望远镜
content.class.visitor.kit.2.name: 燕麦饼
content.class.visitor.name: 访客
content.dlg.guide.approach-albany.opt.0.label: 为何挖三道壕沟？
content.dlg.guide.approach-albany.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.approach-albany.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.approach-albany.text: 奥尔巴尼公爵。国王的兄弟，将近三十年里真正管着苏格兰的那个人。1381年他在里面用印发过一份特许状，可见那时墙已经立起来了，而且他确实在用。
content.dlg.guide.approach-ditches.opt.0.label: 他是谁？
content.dlg.guide.approach-ditches.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.approach-ditches.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.approach-ditches.text: 因为这里是唯一平坦的入口。从别处进来，你都得爬坡，而上面有人守着。想下去就下去吧——壕沟是干的，还凿了台阶，所以你上得来。
content.dlg.guide.approach.opt.0.label: 他是谁？
content.dlg.guide.approach.opt.1.label: 为何挖三道壕沟？
content.dlg.guide.approach.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.approach.text: 进门前先站一会儿，好好看看它。罗伯特·斯图尔特在1380年代把它建在这里，阿多克河汇入泰斯河的地方，北上的路正好经过他门前——这才是关键。这一侧有三道壕沟和一道土堤。其余三面，地势替他守住了。
content.dlg.guide.courtyard-household.text: 公爵住在这里时，大约四十人；他不在时，只有五六人。每个人每天要穿过这座庭院二十来趟——食物往一个方向，水往另一个方向，而守备队一直在你头顶上走来走去。
content.dlg.guide.courtyard-siege.opt.0.label: 谁住在这里？
content.dlg.guide.courtyard-siege.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.courtyard-siege.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.courtyard-siege.text: 这里很少遭围攻，围也围不久。最出名的一夜在1746年：詹姆斯党人占下城堡，俘虏关在楼上，有几个用打结的床单从窗户逃走。其中一人后来还写了出戏说这件事。
content.dlg.guide.courtyard.opt.0.label: 这里遭过围攻吗？
content.dlg.guide.courtyard.opt.1.label: 谁住在这里？
content.dlg.guide.courtyard.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.courtyard.text: 本来四面都要建楼，实际只建起三面。南边那个缺口空了六百年。水井深十八米——围城时真正要紧的是水井，不是城墙。
content.dlg.guide.duchess-hall.opt.0.label: 那个盆是什么？
content.dlg.guide.duchess-hall.opt.1.label: 谁的遗孀？
content.dlg.guide.duchess-hall.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.duchess-hall.text: 她的厅在上面一层，祈祷室就嵌在那边的厚墙里：祭坛、洗圣器的盆、放面包的搁板。1425年，国王在斯特灵处决了公爵的儿子，把杜恩收归王室。打那以后，这里就是一座狩猎行宫，一处孀居宅。
content.dlg.guide.duchess-piscina.opt.0.label: 谁的遗孀？
content.dlg.guide.duchess-piscina.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.duchess-piscina.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.duchess-piscina.text: 这叫圣器洗涤池。祭坛上用过的水不像洗碗水那样随手倒掉——它顺着这个孔流下去，进到城堡自己的地里。旁边的壁龛以前放着面包和葡萄酒，等神父来取。
content.dlg.guide.duchess-queens.opt.0.label: 那个盆是什么？
content.dlg.guide.duchess-queens.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.duchess-queens.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.duchess-queens.text: 前后三位王后，一个接一个。孀居宅就是王后丧了夫、儿媳又想要她那座宫殿时，她去住的地方。她们打猎，在楼下的厅里接见来客，也没动过这里的一砖一石，所以今天还剩下这么多。
content.dlg.guide.gate-garrison.opt.0.label: 铁栅门是什么？
content.dlg.guide.gate-garrison.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.gate-garrison.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.gate-garrison.text: 一个睡在门边的门房，加上公爵那年花钱雇的守备队。你右手边那间归他们住；左手边地板下的坑，关着公爵不花钱养的人。
content.dlg.guide.gate-passage.opt.0.label: 铁栅门是什么？
content.dlg.guide.gate-passage.opt.1.label: 谁守过这里？
content.dlg.guide.gate-passage.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.gate-passage.text: 进去前先抬头看。吊闸收在槽里，铁栅门折回贴在那边墙上，拱顶上那些孔可不是采光用的。这样的路要走二十步，两边各有一间守卫室。
content.dlg.guide.gate-yett.opt.0.label: 谁守过这里？
content.dlg.guide.gate-yett.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.gate-yett.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.gate-yett.text: 铁条编成的格栅门，锻造得让铁条互相交错。你要想取下一根铁条，就得先锯断四根。别处早就不再打造了，苏格兰却还造了很久。
content.dlg.guide.great-hall.opt.0.label: 没有烟囱？
content.dlg.guide.great-hall.opt.1.label: 谁来过这里？
content.dlg.guide.great-hall.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.great-hall.text: 高台上是主桌，其他人沿大厅排开，座次按公爵喜欢的程度定。火生在房间正中央的地上，正上方的屋脊开着个洞。这间房一处烟囱都没有。
content.dlg.guide.hall-louvre.opt.0.label: 谁来过这里？
content.dlg.guide.hall-louvre.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.hall-louvre.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.hall-louvre.text: 烟升上去，从屋脊上那个排烟口散出去，一路把椽子、火腿和每个人的衣服都熏得入了味。人身上带着自家大厅的气味；你凭仆人身上的气味，就能认出是哪一户人家。
content.dlg.guide.hall-montrose.opt.0.label: 没有烟囱？
content.dlg.guide.hall-montrose.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.hall-montrose.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.hall-montrose.text: 1645年，蒙特罗斯驻扎于此，当时战事正酣，这间大厅供他的军官们用餐。这是苏格兰保存最完好的大厅之一，原因很无趣：有钱翻新它的人，没有一个愿意住在这里。
content.dlg.guide.kitchen-oven.opt.0.label: 多少人下厨？
content.dlg.guide.kitchen-oven.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.kitchen-oven.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.kitchen-oven.text: 面包。在炉膛里生火，等火烧尽，把灰耙出来，再把面包坯放在滚烫的石头上。一炉火从热到凉依次做面包、糕点，最后是锅里剩下的东西。
content.dlg.guide.kitchen-staff.opt.0.label: 这烤炉做什么用？
content.dlg.guide.kitchen-staff.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.kitchen-staff.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.kitchen-staff.text: 一个厨子，加上所有他能呼来喝去的人。有转烤肉叉的小工，烤面包日有面包师，还有一个人专门管火。地上的排水口说明了一切——这房间是用水冲的，不是扫的。
content.dlg.guide.kitchen.opt.0.label: 这烤炉做什么用？
content.dlg.guide.kitchen.opt.1.label: 多少人下厨？
content.dlg.guide.kitchen.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.kitchen.text: 两个传菜口。这炉火与公爵餐桌之间就隔着这么点距离，所以厨房才设在这里。壁炉有五米半宽——能在里面烤整头牛，盛宴的日子他们真这么干过。
content.dlg.guide.lords-fireplace.opt.0.label: 这是原物吗？
content.dlg.guide.lords-fireplace.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.lords-fireplace.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.lords-fireplace.text: 这么大的壁炉只砌一座，会把你呛得待不住。并排两座小些的，既能暖了整间屋子，又能让人站在中间——公爵就是这么站的，别人立在穿堂风里向他求事。
content.dlg.guide.lords-hall.opt.0.label: 这是原物吗？
content.dlg.guide.lords-hall.opt.1.label: 为何两座壁炉？
content.dlg.guide.lords-hall.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.lords-hall.text: 公爵自己的厅——留意它在哪儿。就在大门正上方。他坐在自己把着的那道门上头，有自己的楼梯、自己的壁炉；城堡其余部分失守之后，这座塔楼还能自己守下去。
content.dlg.guide.lords-original.opt.0.label: 为何两座壁炉？
content.dlg.guide.lords-original.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.lords-original.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.lords-original.text: 墙是他的。回廊和护墙板是1883年的——一位伯爵把屋顶重新盖上，所以你才能站在房间里，而不是站在长满草的废墟里。
content.dlg.guide.muster-foot.opt.0.label: 他们是谁？
content.dlg.guide.muster-foot.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.muster-foot.opt.2.label: 我们看着。
content.dlg.guide.muster-foot.text: 因为马一向养在城墙外头，从来如此。庭院是让人穿过去的，不是让人在里面骑着转的。再说这座城堡最出名的是什么，你已经听过了，所以你知道路数：没有马。想听马蹄声，你得自己弄出来。
content.dlg.guide.muster-who.opt.0.label: 为何步行？
content.dlg.guide.muster-who.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.muster-who.opt.2.label: 我们看着。
content.dlg.guide.muster-who.text: 公爵的部下。其中二三十人住在门道上方，在你刚走过的大厅里吃饭：一个卫队长、他手下的披甲兵，还有一个从没放过假的门房。卫队长会走到水井边来。其余的人穿过庭院，从地窖门进去——他们一向就是那样去吃晚饭的。
content.dlg.guide.muster.opt.0.label: 他们是谁？
content.dlg.guide.muster.opt.1.label: 为何步行？
content.dlg.guide.muster.opt.2.label: 我们看着。
content.dlg.guide.muster.text: 还有一件事，趁你还没下去。城堡到今天还在每天收工时把卫兵放出来，就像当年门楼上驻着守备队的时候一样。你待在原地，看着庭院。他们会从拱门下面出来。
content.dlg.guide.royal-apartments.opt.0.label: 为何在这上面？
content.dlg.guide.royal-apartments.opt.1.label: 谁的椅子？
content.dlg.guide.royal-apartments.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.royal-apartments.text: 客人睡在厨房上头，因为厨房那面墙是任何城堡里最暖的一面。一间觐见厅，两间卧房，常年备着。苏格兰女王玛丽在杜恩不止住过一回；她儿子的宫廷也来，只要打猎值得跑这一趟。
content.dlg.guide.royal-chair.opt.0.label: 为何在这上面？
content.dlg.guide.royal-chair.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.royal-chair.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.royal-chair.text: 那一周，屋里地位最高的人。椅子上铺的布比椅子本身更要紧——给你看的不是个座位，而是有人有资格坐着，而你只能站着。
content.dlg.guide.royal-warm.opt.0.label: 谁的椅子？
content.dlg.guide.royal-warm.opt.1.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.royal-warm.opt.2.label: 带路吧。
content.dlg.guide.royal-warm.text: 热气向上走。厨房炉火从天不亮一直烧到天黑以后，烟囱的每一块石头都在这面墙的另一边。城堡里住得最好的客人，永远是离做饭最近的那一位。
content.dlg.guide.walk-after.opt.0.label: 哪些电影？
content.dlg.guide.walk-after.opt.1.label: 就这些吗？
content.dlg.guide.walk-after.opt.2.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.walk-after.text: 先是王室，然后是一批伯爵，多半住在别处；1883年屋顶补上，1984年国家接手，从此一直撑着它。六百年，没人真正需要它，也没人真正由它倒下去。
content.dlg.guide.walk-end.opt.0.label: 谢谢你。
content.dlg.guide.walk-end.text: 建起来的，就是这些了。我总在这儿收尾，是为了没建起来的那一样：第四面楼，沿着南墙那一道，图画了，从没动工。六百年，一座庭院少着一面，而从来没有人需要解释为什么。
content.dlg.guide.walk-films.opt.0.label: 后来呢？
content.dlg.guide.walk-films.opt.1.label: 就这些吗？
content.dlg.guide.walk-films.opt.2.label: 返回。
content.dlg.guide.walk-films.text: 一部讲骑士没有马的喜剧。一部剧集里，这座庭院叫临冬城。还有一部穿越爱情剧，带来的游客比那两部哪一部都多。而人们冲我喊的，永远是椰子壳。
content.dlg.guide.wall-walk.opt.0.label: 哪些电影？
content.dlg.guide.wall-walk.opt.1.label: 后来呢？
content.dlg.guide.wall-walk.opt.2.label: 就这些吗？
content.dlg.guide.wall-walk.text: 那是泰斯河，河那头就是苏格兰高地。城墙步道绕城堡整整一圈：守备队在上边，其他人都在下边。而且你早就见过这座城堡，不管你知不知道——摄制组就站在你现在站的地方拍过。
content.fx.wall-walk.done.0.seq.1.0.narrate: 门拱下号角响起，卫兵开始走出来。
content.fx.wall-walk.done.0.seq.2.1.arrive.1.nar: 卫队长在水井边停下，转身面向城墙。

source.dlg.guide.approach-albany.opt.0.label: Why three ditches?
source.dlg.guide.approach-albany.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.approach-albany.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.approach-albany.text: Duke of Albany. The king's brother, and for the best part of thirty years the man who actually ran Scotland. He sealed a charter in there in 1381, so the walls were up by then and he was using them.
source.dlg.guide.approach-ditches.opt.0.label: Who was he?
source.dlg.guide.approach-ditches.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.approach-ditches.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.approach-ditches.text: Because this is the only flat way in. Anywhere else you are coming up a bank with somebody above you. Go down into one if you like — they are dry, and they are cut in steps, so you will get out again.
source.dlg.guide.approach.opt.0.label: Who was he?
source.dlg.guide.approach.opt.1.label: Why three ditches?
source.dlg.guide.approach.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.approach.text: Stand a moment and look at it before we go in. Robert Stewart put this up in the 1380s, where the Ardoch runs into the Teith, and the road north went past his front door — which was the point. Three ditches and a bank on this side. The other three sides the ground does for him.
source.dlg.guide.courtyard-household.text: Forty or so, when the duke was in residence, and half a dozen when he was not. Everyone crossed this yard twenty times a day — food one way, water the other, and the garrison walking over your head the whole time.
source.dlg.guide.courtyard-siege.opt.0.label: Who lived here?
source.dlg.guide.courtyard-siege.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.courtyard-siege.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.courtyard-siege.text: Rarely, and never for long. The famous night here is 1746: the Jacobites held the place and kept prisoners upstairs, and some of them went out of a window on knotted bedsheets. One of them wrote a play about it afterwards.
source.dlg.guide.courtyard.opt.0.label: Was it besieged?
source.dlg.guide.courtyard.opt.1.label: Who lived here?
source.dlg.guide.courtyard.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.courtyard.text: Four ranges were planned. Three were built. That gap on the south side has been a gap for six hundred years. The well is eighteen metres down, and a well is what a siege actually turns on — not the walls.
source.dlg.guide.duchess-hall.opt.0.label: What is the basin?
source.dlg.guide.duchess-hall.opt.1.label: Whose widow?
source.dlg.guide.duchess-hall.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.duchess-hall.text: Her hall, one floor up, and her oratory in the thickness of the wall there: altar, a basin for the vessels, a shelf for the bread. In 1425 the king executed the duke's son at Stirling and took Doune for the crown. After that it was a hunting lodge and a widow's house.
source.dlg.guide.duchess-piscina.opt.0.label: Whose widow?
source.dlg.guide.duchess-piscina.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.duchess-piscina.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.duchess-piscina.text: A piscina. The water used at the altar is not poured away like washing-up water — it goes down that drain and into the ground of the castle itself. The niche beside it held the bread and wine before the priest needed them.
source.dlg.guide.duchess-queens.opt.0.label: What is the basin?
source.dlg.guide.duchess-queens.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.duchess-queens.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.duchess-queens.text: Three of them, one after another. A dower house is where a queen goes when her husband dies and her son's wife wants her palace. They hunted, they held court in the room below, and they left the fabric alone, which is why so much of it is here.
source.dlg.guide.gate-garrison.opt.0.label: What is a yett?
source.dlg.guide.gate-garrison.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.gate-garrison.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.gate-garrison.text: A porter who slept by the door, and whatever garrison the duke was paying that year. The room on your right was theirs. The pit under the floor on the left was for people the duke was not paying.
source.dlg.guide.gate-passage.opt.0.label: What is a yett?
source.dlg.guide.gate-passage.opt.1.label: Who held this?
source.dlg.guide.gate-passage.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.gate-passage.text: Look up before you walk through. Portcullis in its slot, the iron yett folded back against the wall there, and those holes in the vault are not for light. Twenty paces of that, with a guardroom on each side of you.
source.dlg.guide.gate-yett.opt.0.label: Who held this?
source.dlg.guide.gate-yett.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.gate-yett.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.gate-yett.text: A lattice gate of iron bars, forged so the bars pass through one another. You cannot cut a bar out of it without cutting four. Scotland kept making them long after everyone else had given up.
source.dlg.guide.great-hall.opt.0.label: No chimney?
source.dlg.guide.great-hall.opt.1.label: Who came here?
source.dlg.guide.great-hall.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.great-hall.text: High table on the dais, everybody else down the length of the room in order of how much the duke liked them, and the fire in the middle of the floor with a hole in the ridge over it. No chimney anywhere in this room.
source.dlg.guide.hall-louvre.opt.0.label: Who came here?
source.dlg.guide.hall-louvre.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.hall-louvre.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.hall-louvre.text: The smoke goes up and out of the louvre, and on the way it seasons the rafters, the ham and everybody's clothes. People smelled of their own hall. You would know a household by the smell of its servants.
source.dlg.guide.hall-montrose.opt.0.label: No chimney?
source.dlg.guide.hall-montrose.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.hall-montrose.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.hall-montrose.text: Montrose quartered here in 1645, in the middle of the wars, and the hall fed his officers. It is one of the best preserved halls in Scotland, and the reason is dull: nobody rich enough to modernise it ever wanted to live here.
source.dlg.guide.kitchen-oven.opt.0.label: How many cooked?
source.dlg.guide.kitchen-oven.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.kitchen-oven.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.kitchen-oven.text: Bread. You light a fire inside it, let it burn down, rake it out and put the loaves in on the hot stone. One firing does bread, then pastry, then whatever is left in the pot, in that order, as it cools.
source.dlg.guide.kitchen-staff.opt.0.label: What is the oven?
source.dlg.guide.kitchen-staff.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.kitchen-staff.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.kitchen-staff.text: A cook, and whoever the cook could shout at. Spit boys, a baker on baking days, and a man whose whole job was the fire. The drain in the floor tells you the rest of it — this room was washed down, not swept.
source.dlg.guide.kitchen.opt.0.label: What is the oven?
source.dlg.guide.kitchen.opt.1.label: How many cooked?
source.dlg.guide.kitchen.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.kitchen.text: Two hatches. That is the entire distance between this fire and the duke's table, and it is why the kitchen is where it is. The fireplace is five and a half metres across — you could roast an ox in it, and on a feast day they did.
source.dlg.guide.lords-fireplace.opt.0.label: Is this original?
source.dlg.guide.lords-fireplace.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.lords-fireplace.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.lords-fireplace.text: One hearth this size would smoke you out. Two smaller ones side by side heat the room and let you stand between them, which is what the duke did while other people stood in the draught and asked him for things.
source.dlg.guide.lords-hall.opt.0.label: Is this original?
source.dlg.guide.lords-hall.opt.1.label: Why two fires?
source.dlg.guide.lords-hall.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.lords-hall.text: The duke's own hall — and mind where it is. Directly over the gate. He sat above the door he controlled, with his own stair and his own fire, and this tower could hold out after the rest of the castle had gone.
source.dlg.guide.lords-original.opt.0.label: Why two fires?
source.dlg.guide.lords-original.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.lords-original.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.lords-original.text: The walls are his. The gallery and the panelling are 1883 — an earl put the roofs back on, which is the only reason you are standing in a room instead of in a ruin with grass on it.
source.dlg.guide.muster-foot.opt.0.label: Who are they?
source.dlg.guide.muster-foot.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.muster-foot.opt.2.label: We'll watch.
source.dlg.guide.muster-foot.text: Because the horses were stabled outside the walls and always were. A courtyard is for crossing, not for riding about in. And you have already heard what this castle is best known for, so you know the drill: no horses. If you want the sound of them you will have to make it yourself.
source.dlg.guide.muster-who.opt.0.label: Why on foot?
source.dlg.guide.muster-who.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.muster-who.opt.2.label: We'll watch.
source.dlg.guide.muster-who.text: The duke's men. Twenty or thirty of them lived over the gate passage and ate in the hall you walked through: a captain, his men-at-arms, and a porter who never got a day off. The captain comes forward to the well. The rest cross and go in by the cellar door, which is how they always went to their dinner.
source.dlg.guide.muster.opt.0.label: Who are they?
source.dlg.guide.muster.opt.1.label: Why on foot?
source.dlg.guide.muster.opt.2.label: We'll watch.
source.dlg.guide.muster.text: One thing more before you go down. The castle still turns its guard out at the end of the day, the way it did when there was a garrison over that gate. Stay where you are and watch the courtyard. They come out under the arch.
source.dlg.guide.royal-apartments.opt.0.label: Why up here?
source.dlg.guide.royal-apartments.opt.1.label: Whose chair?
source.dlg.guide.royal-apartments.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.royal-apartments.text: Guests slept over the kitchen, because the kitchen is the warmest wall in any castle. An audience chamber and two bedchambers, kept ready. Mary, Queen of Scots stayed at Doune more than once; so did her son's court, when the hunting was worth the ride.
source.dlg.guide.royal-chair.opt.0.label: Why up here?
source.dlg.guide.royal-chair.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.royal-chair.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.royal-chair.text: Whoever outranked everyone else in the room that week. The cloth over it matters more than the chair — you were not being shown a seat, you were being shown that somebody was entitled to sit while you stood.
source.dlg.guide.royal-warm.opt.0.label: Whose chair?
source.dlg.guide.royal-warm.opt.1.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.royal-warm.opt.2.label: Lead on.
source.dlg.guide.royal-warm.text: Heat goes up. The kitchen fire burns from before dawn to after dark, and every stone of that chimney is on the other side of this wall. The best-lodged guest in a castle is always the one nearest the cooking.
source.dlg.guide.walk-after.opt.0.label: Which films?
source.dlg.guide.walk-after.opt.1.label: Is that everything?
source.dlg.guide.walk-after.opt.2.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.walk-after.text: Crown, then earls who mostly lived elsewhere, then the roofs in 1883, then the state took it on in 1984 and has kept it standing since. Six hundred years of nobody quite needing it and nobody quite letting it fall.
source.dlg.guide.walk-end.opt.0.label: Thank you.
source.dlg.guide.walk-end.text: That is everything that was built. I always finish here because of what is not: the fourth range, along that south wall, drawn and never begun. Six hundred years of a courtyard with one side missing, and nobody has ever had to explain why.
source.dlg.guide.walk-films.opt.0.label: And after?
source.dlg.guide.walk-films.opt.1.label: Is that everything?
source.dlg.guide.walk-films.opt.2.label: Back.
source.dlg.guide.walk-films.text: A comedy about knights who have no horses. A series where this courtyard was a place called Winterfell. And a time-travel romance that brought more visitors than either. It is the coconuts people shout at me about.
source.dlg.guide.wall-walk.opt.0.label: Which films?
source.dlg.guide.wall-walk.opt.1.label: And after?
source.dlg.guide.wall-walk.opt.2.label: Is that everything?
source.dlg.guide.wall-walk.text: That is the Teith, and those are the Highlands behind it. The walk goes the whole way round: garrison up here, everybody else down there. And you have seen this castle before, whether you know it or not — film crews have stood where you are standing.
source.fx.wall-walk.done.0.seq.1.0.narrate: A horn goes off under the gate arch, and the guard begins to come out.
source.fx.wall-walk.done.0.seq.2.1.arrive.1.nar: The captain halts by the well and turns to face the wall.
